methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native represent grassroots peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could build distributed fluency outside traditional tech hubs, directly counteracting concentration dynamics.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke signals intentional capability-building in a non-metro region, suggesting infrastructure for distributed AI fluency rather than passive platform consumption or exclusion from the AI economy.

signals.title: AI is already common in Virginia Beach high schools. Leaders weigh guardrails - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: AI already embedded in Virginia Beach high schools indicates broad but shallow adoption via educational platforms—widespread access without deep technical capability development, fitting the platform-delivered distribution model.

signals.title: UVA President Scott Beardsley charts University’s future in artificial intelligence - UVA Today
signals.signal_reading: UVA's strategic AI positioning signals institutional concentration of deep capability in flagship research universities, potentially widening the gap between academic centers and communities without similar anchor institutions.

signals.title: Rural advocacy groups band together to oppose data centers, related energy projects
signals.signal_reading: Rural coalitions opposing data centers reveal infrastructure conflicts where regions bear energy burdens without gaining AI capability—physical concentration of infrastructure without knowledge distribution, reinforcing exclusion.
